about: Reference films for the bassline skill, ranked by the user's verdict. Study the best first; treat the caveats as things not to repeat.

films.user_said: very wonderful work, I am very impressed
films.made_by: Claude in the main thread, from Claude's own script
what_works: One object carried through every act: paragraph rows -> grooves -> river -> face
Personal subject Claude actually has a view on (being summarized)
Literal paper puns on each quoted phrase (fold, stamp, tear, selection box)
Tiny specific character: a caret with one eye that blinks and types
Callback ending: the face becomes one card in a new ribbon
caveats: Calm, contemplative pace; a good model for feeling, less so for energy

films.made_by: Claude in the main thread; script inspired by a roon (@tszzl) post about pretraining being like building steam engines before thermodynamics
what_works: Built for energy: short-short-BANG script, workshop rhythm that accelerates, a beat of silence before 'ran', band slams in
Full-frame hits on 'I run.' and 'I pull.' with brass stabs
Chalk theory arrives slightly wrong and snaps exactly onto the engine on 'oh.'
caveats: Reads more like a sequence of good gags than one continuous transformation; the engine carries through but the acts don't morph into each other the way Riverbed's do
Characters and the race are small in frame for stretches
Sound mix never checked by ear

films.verdict: decent narration, pretty good visuals, but lacked oomph
films.made_by: A fresh subagent using only the skill (a cold test of SKILL.md); script inspired by a roon post about saddle points in high-dimensional loss landscapes
what_works: Clever concept true to its source (gradient descent: valleys are really saddles)
Contour-map unfold and the stepped-hill callback ending
caveats: Not enough energy: the narration is a calm explanation of standing still, and the subject (being parked) works against momentum
The narrator (a blue paper ball) is too small for most of the film
The saddle drawing is hard to read; the torn front view reads as a brown lump
Explains an idea rather than driving one; avoid lecture-shaped scripts
